facts.title: Charles Aznavour
facts.text: More than a thousand songs written or co-written, nearly thirteen hundred tracks recorded in multiple languages.

facts.title: A survivor's son
facts.text: His mother, Knar Baghdassarian, was a survivor of the Armenian genocide. He was born Shahnour Vaghinak Aznavourian.

facts.title: A family that hid others
facts.text: They hid Jews and Armenians in their apartment, including resistance fighters Mélinée and Missak Manouchian.

facts.title: Noticed by Édith Piaf
facts.text: His duo with pianist Pierre Roche went on tour with her and Les Compagnons de la chanson.

facts.title: December 12, 1960
facts.text: Singing “Je m'voyais déjà” with his back to the audience, he won over a frigid room. He was 36.

facts.title: “Pour toi Arménie”
facts.text: The 1989 charity song, recorded with dozens of artists, topped the charts.

facts.title: National Hero of Armenia
facts.text: In 2009 he became Armenia's ambassador to Switzerland and permanent representative to the UN in Geneva.

ytTitle: Charles Aznavour, from Paris to National Hero of Armenia
ytLead: Son of an Armenian genocide survivor, Charles Aznavour wrote or co-wrote more than a thousand songs, then served Armenia as an ambassador and was named its National Hero.
